messages.subject_clean: ggvis Question
messages.body_plain:
I feel like there's an obvious answer to this problem, but I'm not finding it.

I'm having trouble using ggvis interactively with shiny controls (inside of a shiny document).

Here's a super simplified example of the code chunk that's causing problems:

```{r, echo=FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(ggvis)

inputPanel(
  sliderInput("multiplier", label = "Multiplier",
              value = 1, min = 0.5, max = 2, step = 0.5)
)

reactive({  mtcars %>%
                    mutate(wtTwo = wt*input$multiplier) %>%
                    ggvis(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg) %>%
                    layer_points()
             }) %>% bind_shiny("example")

ggvisOutput("example")

```

When I run the code, I get an error that says "wrong result size (0), expected 32 or 1."
I'm pretty sure the problem is occurring with ggvis and not dplyr, because the following works fine:

renderTable({
            mtcars %>%
                 mutate(wt = wt*input$multiplier)
             })

Thanks for the help and happy New Year!

messages.body_plain:
I have a shiny App and would like to add a "Reset" button to clear all inputs. This is particularly useful if one has several inputs and does not want to reset each manually.

I tried the idea given [here](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/24265980/reset-inputs-button-in-shiny-app).
It somewhat works in a buggy way:
- for some reason it prints the names of the variables above the reset button, ie. "categ_1", "date", "categ_2".
- Also, I don't know how to combine update & uiOutput in the below line:

     output$resetable_input <- renderUI({
             times <- input$reset_input
             div(
               id=letters[(times %% length(letters)) + 1],
               #                updateuiOutput(session,"firm"),
               updateSelectInput(session,"categ_1",
                                 choices = c("All",unique(as.character(df$CATEG_1)))),
               updateSelectInput(session,"date",
                                 choices = c("All","Last 28 Days","Last Quarter")),
               updateSelectInput(session,"categ_2",
                                 choices = c("All",unique(as.character(df$CATEG_2))))
             )
           })

Has anyone found an easy way to do this?

Many Thanks in advance!

1. Create sample data

          set.seed(1)
          df <- data.frame(FIRM=rep(LETTERS[1:7],each=10), CATEG_1=rbinom(70,4,0.9),CATEG_2=rbinom(70,1,0.2),date=as.Date("2014-01-01")+1:10,y1=sample(1:100,70))

2. shiny App

         library(shiny)
         library(rCharts)
         library(doBy)
         library(plyr)

          shinyApp(ui =
           shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

             # Application title
             headerPanel("Example"),

             sidebarPanel(
               uiOutput("firm"),
               #  selectInput("firm", "Filter by firm:",
               #   choices = unique(as.character(df))),
               selectInput("categ_1", "Filter by Category 1:",
                           choices = c("All",unique(as.character(df$CATEG_1)))),
               selectInput("date", "Filter by Date:",
                           choices = c("All","Last 28 Days","Last Quarter")),
               selectInput("categ_2", "Filter by Category 2:",
                           choices = c("All",unique(as.character(df$CATEG_2)))),
               uiOutput('resetable_input'),
               actionButton("reset_input", "Reset inputs")
             ), #sidebarPanel

             mainPanel(
               h4("Example plot",style = "color:grey"),
               showOutput("plot", "nvd3")
             ) # mainPanel
           ) #sidebarLayout
           ) #shinyU
         ,
         server = shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

           subset_data <- reactive({df <- filter_data(df,input$firm,
                                                      input$date,
                                                      input$categ_1,
                                                      input$categ_2)
                                    shiny::validate(need(!is.null(df),"No data to display"))
                                    return(df)})

           output$firm <- renderUI({
             input$date
             input$categ_1
             input$categ_2
             selectInput("firm", "Filter by Firm:",
                         choices = c("All",as.character(unique(isolate(subset_data()$FIRM)))))
           })

              output$resetable_input <- renderUI({
             times <- input$reset_input
             div(
               id=letters[(times %% length(letters)) + 1],
               #                updateuiOutput(session,"firm"),
               updateSelectInput(session,"categ_1",
                                 choices = c("All",unique(as.character(df$CATEG_1)))),
               updateSelectInput(session,"date",
                                 choices = c("All","Last 28 Days","Last Quarter")),
               updateSelectInput(session,"categ_2",
                                 choices = c("All",unique(as.character(df$CATEG_2))))
             )
           })

           output$plot<-renderChart2({ build_plot(subset_data()) })

           ##############
           #below are the functions used in the code
           ##############

           # function for date subsetting

           filter_date<-function(df,dateRange="All"){
             filt <- df
             td <- max(as.Date(filt$date))
             if (dateRange=='Last 28 Days'){filt <-filt[filt$date>=(td-28),]}
             if (dateRange=='Last Quarter'){filt <-filt[filt$date>=(td-84),]}
             return(filt)
           }  # filter by date

           # function for data subsetting

           filter_data<-function(df,firm=NULL,dateRange="All",categ_1=NULL,categ_2=NULL)
           {
             filt<-filter_date(df,dateRange)

             if (!is.null(firm)) {
               if(firm!='All') {filt <- filt[filt$FIRM==firm,]}
             }
             if (!is.null(categ_1)){
               if (categ_1!='All') {filt <- filt[filt$CATEG_1==categ_1,]}
             }
             if (!is.null(categ_2)) {
               if (categ_2!='All') {filt <- filt[filt$CATEG_2==categ_2,]}
             }

             if(nrow(filt)==0) {filt <- NULL}
             return(filt)
           } # prepare data to be plotted

           # function to create plot

           build_plot <- function(df) {
             plotData<-df
             # If 1 partner selected, time series is shown
             if (length(as.character(unique(plotData$FIRM)))==1) {

               tabledta<-summaryBy(y1~FIRM+date,data=plotData,FUN=sum,keep.names=TRUE)

               filler = expand.grid(FIRM=as.character(unique(df$FIRM)),
                                    date=seq(min(tabledta$date),max(tabledta$date),by='1 day'))
               df = merge(filler,
                          tabledta,
                          by=c('date','FIRM'),
                          all.x=T)
               df[is.na <http://is.na>(df)]=0
               p <- nPlot(y1 ~ date, group = 'FIRM', data = df, type = 'lineChart')
               p$chart(margin=list(left=150))
               p$yAxis(showMaxMin = FALSE)
               p$xAxis(tickFormat ="#!function(d) {return d3.time.format('%Y-%m-%d')(new Date(d * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));}!#")
               p
             }
             # If "All" partners are selected, barchart of Top 5 is shown
             else{
               SummaryTab<-aggregate(y1~FIRM,data=plotData,FUN=sum)
               SummaryTab$rank=rank(SummaryTab$y1)
               SummaryTab$rank[SummaryTab$rank>5]<-6

               if (length(SummaryTab$rank)>5) {
                 #Top 5 partners in terms of y1 are shown
                 top5<-SummaryTab[SummaryTab$rank<=5,]
                 # other partners are collapsed, shown as 1 entry

                 others<-aggregate(y1~rank,data=SummaryTab,FUN=sum)
                 others<-others[others$rank==6,]
                 others$FIRM<-"Others"

                 # Create the summarytable to be plotted
                 plotData=rbind(top5,others)}

               tabledta<-summaryBy(y1~FIRM,data=plotData,FUN=sum,keep.names=TRUE)
               tabledta<-arrange(tabledta,y1)
               #   if(is.null(tabledta)) {print("Input is an empty string")}

               p <- nPlot(y1 ~ FIRM,data = tabledta, type = 'multiBarHorizontalChart')
               p$chart(margin=list(left=150))
               p$yAxis(showMaxMin = FALSE)
               p
             }

           }
         }) #shinyServer
          )

messages.subject: scroll panels in a shiny app

messages.body_plain:
My shiny app (ClinicalTrialDesignExperimenter)
needs a scrollable panel below some fixed items.
I wrestled with this for a long time.
Using <div style="overflow-y: auto; max-height: 400px;" >
worked great in Firefox, but in Chrome and Safari the content of the panel
did not show up.  (The scrolling content would flash then disappear.)

I just stumbled on an answer.
I placed the following between the fixed content above
and the scrolling panel below:
    HTML(' ')
Any "visible" content will do...
for example I now use
   tagAppendAttributes(em( textOutput("SCENARIO_TREE_label"), class="clickMeToClearSelection"))
you could replace the nbsp with any string for example,
but interposing br() or hr()  instead
is not sufficient to solve the problem.

The "fixed" stuff above ended with a series of conditional panels.
With a little experimenting it seems that's the cause of the problem.
Thus the immediate predecessor of the panel must be not conditional.

Maybe this note will save somebody vast numbers of google hours.

messages.subject: Re: Using sendInputMessage and receiveMessage to make shiny input objects reactive
messages.subject_clean: Using sendInputMessage and receiveMessage to make shiny input objects reactive
messages.body_plain:
I solved this problem with the help of Ivan the jstree guru.
I'd been confused between different jstree  versions.

There is only one way currently to make a jstree version 3.0
reactive (in the javascript, not R shiny, sense),
by creating the jstree with a core:data clause:
 $("#jstreeScenario").jstree(
{ core: { data: function(node, cb) { cb(theJsonMessage); }},
       ...
);
Then from R use session$sendInputMessage
to send the tree's new JSON into the javascript receiver,
where you get
> $.extend(ss_jstree, {
>   receiveMessage: function(el, inputMessage) {
>     message = inputMessage;
>     // clean up the message
>     message = message.replace(/..."is.logical..."/g, "is.logical");
>     message = message.replace(/..."is.numeric..."/g, "is.numeric");
>     message = message.replace(/\\"/g, '"');
>     message = message.replace(/'/g, "");
>     message = message.replace(/^ *\[1\] *"/, "");
>     message = message.replace(/.$/, "");
>     theJsonMessage = eval(message);
> ...

After assigning to theJsonMessage, the tree appearance automatically refreshes.
This is working now in ClinicalTrialDesignExperimenter.
The message cleanup is needed to make sure various special characters
don't mess up the JSON; the details will depend on what non-alphanumeric characters
appear in your tree. The cleanup you see above is fine for my stuff;
I'm sure it's not sufficient for all cases.

I've left out some details, like how to assemble the message to pass
via session$sendInputMessage.
If interested, refer to ClinicalTrialDesignExperimenter on github,
and check out these files inside the folder  inst/shinyInterface/:
    jstreeScenarioContent.html
    www.ss-jstree.js
    ui.R  & search for jstreeScenario
    server.R & search for observerCurrentScenario

I'm not really using shinysky's jstree,
but my customized version which was inspired by it. (Thanks, Xiaodaigh.)
The shinyTree package is now at cran, I think,
and maybe it solves these problems, but too late for me.

>

>

> That works fine, but then the ability to select a node in the tree vanishes.

> More details from the jstree angle are here:

messages.body_plain:
The way I implemented a similar functionality in my app is a bit more complex.  It would be great if somebody else will comment with their methods, especially if simpler / better than mine -:)

In my case, a number of things need to occur every time somebody press a Save button.

Shiny has an action button that is incremented by one every time it is pressed. This is how I check if it has been pressed:

observe({
    # this line of code covers the first occurrence
    if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
    # this is to get the value of the button, but
    # actually do something only when it has been pressed (+ 1)
    if(input$saveButton < valPpu$buttonF) { return() }
    valPpu$buttonF <- valPpu$buttonF + 1
})

Please note that valPpu is a reactive variable.  I use it to build "flags" that will be read by other part of the app (other reactive or render functions).

A render function depending on the button will look like:

output$xyz  <- renderSomething({
if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
  .... more code here ...
 if(input$saveButton < valPpu$buttonF) {
 # ignore: the button has not been pressed!
....  more code here
} else {
# This will make sure this part of the code is not run next time
valPpu$buttonF <- input$saveButton
....  more code here
})

This makes the rendering function to react when the button is pressed, but making sure that any action is performed only once.

messages.subject: Re: Using reactive function 'recursively' - updating data as many times as user presses action button
messages.subject_clean: Using reactive function 'recursively' - updating data as many times as user presses action button
messages.body_plain:
You could do something like this, where df is stored outside the reactive and modified each time:

df <- NULL
data <- reactive({
  df <<- foo(df, input$var1, input$var2)
  df
})

A more properly reactive solution would use reactiveValues. A reactiveValues object is just like the input object, so when you change values in it, it will invalidate all downstream reactives and cause them to re-execute:

vals <- reactiveValues()
vals$df <- NULL

observe({
  v$df <<- foo(isolate(v$df), input$var1, input$var2)
})

# Then you can access v$df as just like an input$xx value
output$table <- renderTable({
  v$df
})

Here's a working example of the latter, using an actionButton:

shinyApp(
  ui = bootstrapPage(
    actionButton("goButton", "Go!"),
    tableOutput("table")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    vals <- reactiveValues()
    vals$df <- data.frame(x = numeric(0), y = numeric(0))

    # Add observer to watch for changes to input$goButton and update vals$df
    observe({
      vals$df <<- rbind(
        isolate(vals$df),
        data.frame(x=input$goButton, y=input$goButton)
      )
      # Need to isolate vals$df so we don't end up in infinite loop with vals$df
      # triggering this observer over and over.
    })

    # Then you can access vals$df as just like an input$xx value
    output$table <- renderTable({
      vals$df
    })
  }
)

-Winston

Hi Albert and Jose,

Thanks, that was incredibly helpful, particularly Albert's reply! I just realised that the progress bar is now a feature in the shiny package itself and the syntax has altered somewhat, so after updating the syntax my app runs fine! Much thanks!

Regards,
Jin Rou (JR)

On Friday, December 26, 2014 7:02:51 AM UTC-5, Albert Jay wrote:
> Hello
>
> I had the same problem when I updated shinyIncubator() on my laptop.
>
> private$min is a variable within the progressbars you get in shinyIncubator, see here:
>
> https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator
>
> I would imagine you have different versions of shinyIncubator on your local server and on ShinyApps.io.  A good test would be to get rid of your progress bar(s) and re-test the code.  If it's the problem, re-code your progress bars for the new syntax accordingly.
>
> Thanks
>
> On Tuesday, December 23, 2014 10:53:43 PM UTC, Jin Rou New wrote:

> >
> > I have an app that works fine without errors locally and on ShinyApps.io, however, I get the following error when I upload it to my server that runs Shiny Server:
> >
> > Error: non-numeric argument to binary operator
> >
> > Error log:
> > >
> > > Warning in is.na <http://is.na>(value) :
> > >

> >
> > - JR

the help page of ?DT::datatable, and it will be clearer if you can
post a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example that shows
what you expect, otherwise it is a little bit hard to read your mind.

http://rstudio.github.io/DT/ It did not give you exactly the example
of coloring, but it should be straightforward to adapt it if you are
familiar with JavaScript/jQuery.

messages.body_plain:
There could be multiple issues in this post:

First, please do not try shiny < 0.10.1. That will only waste your
time. The article http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/unicode.html
stated clearly that the support was only available since shiny 0.10.1.
The next time if you want to try anything, please start from the
latest CRAN release. If that does not work, try
devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny') to see if the problem still
exists; if it does, it is time to report to us. We certainly
appreciate it if you test multiple previous versions, but sometimes it
is probably not worth it.

Your Windows locale is English_United States.1252, which means you are
unlikely to be able to run that example by definition, since the
example uses Simplified Chinese characters. To run it, you may have to
change your system locale to Simplified Chinese (go to the Control
Panel -> Region and Language -> find the button to change the locale;
you can keep the display language as English, unless you can read
Chinese).

You said you "copied" the example, and copying text does not guarantee
what its encoding will be under Windows. You should download the
example from https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples You can either
clone the GIT repo, or just download it if you do not know GIT:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/archive/master.zip Then
unzip it, and run the example 022. This guarantees you will not change
the original encoding by accident. If your OS does not support Chinese
characters, it will not work even if you save the file as UTF-8.

Once you are in a Chinese locale, makes sure the file encoding is
UTF-8, **and** have Chinese fonts available (to show Chinese
characters in the plot), you should be able to run the example under
Windows.

For Ubuntu, the encoding is not an issue (the default locale is often
base on UTF-8). I'm surprised that the example did not work. I suspect
you copied the files from Windows, instead of using our original
example files in the Github repo.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: How to manage cond. formatting & checkboxes with the new package DT?
messages.subject_clean: How to manage cond. formatting & checkboxes with the new package DT?
messages.body_plain:
Please find a simplified code attached.
Rather than use a checkboxGroupInput element it would look better to have the picker in the actual data table, but I'm not sure how to do this.
Next step would be use conditional formatting on the table: e.g. any entry changed by the sliders below
a threshold could be amber or red,  but also in this case I'm not sure how to do this.
library(shiny)
library(data.table)

#
dt_ = data.table( Month = month.abb[1:5],
A=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4),
B=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4),
C=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4),
D=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4),
E=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4))

dt_[,id :=.I]
dt <- copy(dt_)
setkey(dt_, "Month")
setkey(dt, "Month")

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
fluidRow(
  column(4,
    actionButton("saveButton", "Update Model"))),
fluidRow(
  column(6, dataTableOutput('DT')),
  column(3, br(),br(),checkboxGroupInput("pick",h6("Picker"),
    month.abb[1:5])),
  column(3, uiOutput('foo'))),
fluidRow(
  column(4, verbatimTextOutput('vals')))
  ),

  server = function(session,input, output) {
    valPpu <- reactiveValues()

    valPpu$buttonF <- 1
##
  output$DT <- renderDataTable({
  if(length(input$pick) > 0 ) {

    labs <- isolate( input$pick )
    buttn <- isolate( valPpu$buttonF )
    iter <- length(labs)
    valLabs <- sapply(1:iter, function(i) {
            as.numeric(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]]) })

    if( iter == sum(sapply(valLabs,length)) ) {

          cPerc <- valLabs
          cPerc <- as.data.table(cPerc)
          cPercDt <- cbind(Month=labs,cPerc)

          ival <- which(dt[["Month"]]
              %in% cPercDt[["Month"]])
          setkey(cPercDt, "Month")
          for(j in LETTERS[1:5]) set(dt_, i=ival,
          j=j, dt[cPercDt][[j]] * (1 + dt_[cPercDt][["cPerc"]]) )

  } }

  dt_[order(id),]
  }, options = list(
  scrollX = TRUE,
  scrollY = "250px" ,
  scrollCollapse = TRUE,
  paging = FALSE,
  searching = FALSE,
  ordering = FALSE )
)
##
  output$foo <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
    if(length(input$pick) > 0 ) {
      iter <- length(input$pick)
      buttn <- isolate( valPpu$buttonF )
      valLabs <- sapply(1:iter, function(i) {
      if(is.null(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]] )) {
                0
      } else {  as.numeric(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]])  }
      })
  #
  toRender <- lapply(1:iter, function(i) {
    sliderInput(inputId = paste0(month.abb[i], "_v",buttn),
                label =  h6(paste0(month.abb[i],"")),
                min = -1,
                max = 1,
                step = 0.01,
                value = valLabs[i],
                format = "##0.#%",
                locale = "gb", ticks = FALSE, animate = FALSE)
                })

      toRender
    }
    })

    observe({

  if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
  if(input$saveButton < valPpu$buttonF) { return() }
  valPpu$buttonF <- valPpu$buttonF + 1
# TODO: saving code
})
  }
)

> Please find a simplified code attached.
> Rather than use a checkboxGroupInput element it would look better to have the picker in the actual data table, but I'm not sure how to do this.
> Next step would be use conditional formatting on the table: e.g. any entry changed by the sliders below
> a threshold could be amber or red,  but also in this case I'm not sure how to do this.
> library(shiny)
> library(data.table)
>
> #

> E=rnorm(5, mean = 5, sd = 4))
>
> dt_[,id :=.I]
> dt <- copy(dt_)
> setkey(dt_, "Month")
> setkey(dt, "Month")
>
> shinyApp(
>   ui = fluidPage(

>   column(4,

> fluidRow(
>   column(4, verbatimTextOutput('vals')))
>   ),
>
>   server = function(session,input, output) {
>     valPpu <- reactiveValues()
>
>     valPpu$buttonF <- 1
> ##
>   output$DT <- renderDataTable({
>   if(length(input$pick) > 0 ) {
>
>     labs <- isolate( input$pick )
>     buttn <- isolate( valPpu$buttonF )

>     valLabs <- sapply(1:iter, function(i) {
>             as.numeric(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]]) })
>
>     if( iter == sum(sapply(valLabs,length)) ) {
>
>           cPerc <- valLabs
>           cPerc <- as.data.table(cPerc)
>           cPercDt <- cbind(Month=labs,cPerc)
>
>           ival <- which(dt[["Month"]]
>               %in% cPercDt[["Month"]])
>           setkey(cPercDt, "Month")
>           for(j in LETTERS[1:5]) set(dt_, i=ival,
>           j=j, dt[cPercDt][[j]] * (1 + dt_[cPercDt][["cPerc"]]) )
>
>   } }
>
>   dt_[order(id),]
>   }, options = list(
>   scrollX = TRUE,
>   scrollY = "250px" ,
>   scrollCollapse = TRUE,
>   paging = FALSE,
>   searching = FALSE,
>   ordering = FALSE )
> )

>     if(length(input$pick) > 0 ) {
>       iter <- length(input$pick)
>       buttn <- isolate( valPpu$buttonF )
>       valLabs <- sapply(1:iter, function(i) {
>       if(is.null(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]] )) {
>                 0
>       } else {  as.numeric(input[[paste0(month.abb[i],"_v",buttn)]])  }
>       })
>   #

>     sliderInput(inputId = paste0(month.abb[i], "_v",buttn),

>                 min = -1,
>                 max = 1,
>                 step = 0.01,
>                 value = valLabs[i],
>                 format = "##0.#%",
>                 locale = "gb", ticks = FALSE, animate = FALSE)
>                 })
>
>       toRender
>     }
>     })
>
>
>     observe({
>
>   if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
>   if(input$saveButton < valPpu$buttonF) { return() }
>   valPpu$buttonF <- valPpu$buttonF + 1
> # TODO: saving code
> })
>   }
> )
>
>

messages.subject: Re: How to? Infinite scroll in DataTables for shiny 10.2 and above
messages.subject_clean: How to? Infinite scroll in DataTables for shiny 10.2 and above
messages.body_plain:
According to http://legacy.datatables.net/ref, this option has been
deprecated, and replaced by sScrollY later. Then DataTables 1.10.x
replaced it by scrollY: https://datatables.net/upgrade/1.10-convert
Then what you should really look at is:
http://datatables.net/reference/option/scrollY

Here is a minimal example:

library(shiny)
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(fluidRow(dataTableOutput('foo'))),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$foo = renderDataTable({
      iris
    }, options = list(
      scrollY = '300px', paging = FALSE
    ))
  }
)

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: deleting current element in selectizeInput box causes severe error
messages.subject_clean: deleting current element in selectizeInput box causes severe error
messages.body_plain:
> Is there some way to defer processing until the item has really been identified/selected?

This is what validate/need <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html> was designed for (pass FALSE as the message). It means that the outputs that rely on this input will go blank though.

If you really don't want that, you can use a reactiveValues and observer; instead of referring directly to the input, refer to a reactiveValues value, and set up an observer to only update the reactiveValues using the input IF the input is non-empty. (However, I think this would look kind of confusing in the UI if you deleted the selected value and nothing actually changed.)

messages.body_plain:
This gets even weirder. I changed the app a bit to try to see whether any unicode chars render, and found that some do on my computer. In the process, though, I lost the displayed unicode characters on shinyApps.io.

Updated gist <https://gist.github.com/srvanderplas/4b2eb3ae062ab2ae96cd>
ShinyApps.io <https://srvanderplas.shinyapps.io/UnicodeExample/>
My local server <http://vanderplas.dyndns-remote.com/Shiny/WorkingExampleUnicodeChars/>

Both versions are outputting sessionInfo() and Sys.info() to the UI, so that should help a bit.

At this point, my best guess is some sort of encoding/locale issue, but when I set the locale in R directly on my machine, it still doesn't seem to work. Certain characters display, though - try starting at 0630, for instance, or 2630. I can't get them now, but at one point I also had nordic runes. I have no idea what changed, though.

As a side note, I tried adding a png render of the same plot to the shiny app, but can't get the png image to display, despite following almost exactly the example in renderImage(). Not sure what's up there.

I'd be ok using renderImage() as a workaround if it would actually work, but that doesn't seem to be the case.

I'm not sure exactly what you mean by

>  isolate Shiny and Shiny Server from this issue.

Since both the output and printing to PNG/PDF work on my machine (removing both shiny and shiny server from the equation), but adding Shiny into the equation makes the points not render, I'm not sure how to remove them from the equation.

>From ggplot2 in Rstudio (sans Shiny)

Thanks for the help!
Susan

I guess you can compose the JavaScript object using R string functions
like paste(), e.g.

addMarkers(..., icon = JS(paste('L.icon({
  iconUrl:', x, ',
  iconSize: [40, 40]

where you decide what x is.

messages.body_plain:
To remove shiny/shiny server from the equation, you simply do not use
them at all, e.g. ssh into the server, open R, open a png() device (or
Cairo::CairoPNG()), draw the plot, close the device, quit R, and
retrieve the png file. You do not have to draw a plot using shiny,
right?

Yihui

I have attached my files.  If anyone can point me in the right direction I would appreciate it.

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Hello, thanks for your reply.

While your example scrolls the whole table, it is not what I am looking for. You loaded the whole table on one page, which could become troublesome when you use very large tables.

What I was looking for is and working implementation of this new DataTable syntax in shiny: https://datatables.net/extensions/scroller/

It seems pretty cool...

Am Dienstag, 6. Januar 2015 17:56:06 UTC+1 schrieb Yihui Xie:
> According to http://legacy.datatables.net/ref, this option has been
> deprecated, and replaced by sScrollY later. Then DataTables 1.10.x
> replaced it by scrollY: https://datatables.net/upgrade/1.10-convert
> Then what you should really look at is:
> http://datatables.net/reference/option/scrollY
>
> Here is a minimal example:
>
> library(shiny)
> shinyApp(
>   ui = fluidPage(fluidRow(dataTableOutput('foo'))),
>   server = function(input, output) {
>     output$foo = renderDataTable({
>       iris
>     }, options = list(
>       scrollY = '300px', paging = FALSE
>     ))
>   }
> )
>
> Regards,
> Yihui
>
>

messages.body_plain:
Holy shit, I fixed it with one line of code:

options(RCurlOptions = list(cainfo = system.file("CurlSSL", "cacert.pem", package = "RCurl")))

I'm not even sure what that means, but it was on a discussion board about someone getting a similar error when they tried to get stuff off of Twitter on a mac.  They said, "I tried this code that was supposed to work for Windows, but it didn't work for me."

I tried it anyway and it work.  Hallelujah.
Thanks for all of you help.
S

messages.body_plain:
Hi Yihui,

Thanks for your reply, but there is no need to use print().

In fact my problem was due to a bug in shiny.

I'm working on windows 7 and:
- I've chosen to launch my app directly on my browser (google chrome) => nothing appear from a combination of 2 ggplots on a renderPlot().
- I've chosen to launch my app on a RStudio window (which is very bad considering the rendering of the app and the fact that it does not keep track of my current working directory) => it's working perfectly well.
- I've deployed my app on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> => it's working perfectly well.

So as always with shiny lots of bad luck can make you waste a lot of time...

Regards

Le jeudi 8 janvier 2015 01:27:53 UTC+4, Yihui Xie a écrit :
> Chances are you forgot to print() the result.
>
> Regards,
> Yihui
>
>

> >
> > I've try to combine two ggplots with arrangeGrob(), grid.arrange() and

> > No errors are generated, but nothing appears on my tab !
> >
> > So could anybody confirm me that this is actually not possible ?
> > Is there another procedure to follow ?
> >
> > Thanks

messages.subject: Application stops unexpectedly
messages.subject_clean: Application stops unexpectedly
messages.body_plain:
I have recently returned to my shiny-server installation after a long absence. The apps were all written (and successfully deployed on a local server) about 18 months ago.

In the past week I have rebuilt my server which is now running UBUNTU 14.04 and the latest shiny-server.

I copied my previous apps across to the /srv/shiny-server/ folder and have verified they work by successfully running them from within R-studio.

The problem is when I try to run them from a browser either on the LAN or WAN I get the error message: "The application unexpectedly exited. Diagnostic information has been dumped to the JavaScript error console".

I realize this issue has been raised and discussed previously. One suggested fix was to increase the app time-out settings in the shiny-server.conf file which I did but to no effect.

The message is not generated immediately - the app is clearly running as it displays some of the ui.R stuff header, tabs, slider bars drop down lists etc.) but seems to come to a halt about the point where a plot is to be displayed. I was thinking this may be a permission issue and so changed the folder and ui.R and server.R permissions to 777. However this did not resolve the issue.

You are welcome to run the app yourself. It can be accessed at: http://bit.ly/1xSntVU

Any suggestions most welcome.

Cheers,
David.

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Ah thanks ZJ for catching that, silly error on my part. I've fixed that bug (updated code below) but the alert still does not show up and there are no error messages.

What I've tried to debug this:
1. When I replace bsAlert(inputId = "alert_anchor") in server.R with a block of text like p("error"), the text shows up when Show alert = TRUE, so the dynamic UI does work as expected.
2. When I insert bsAlert(inputId = "alert_anchor") in ui.R instead of wrapping it in renderUI and using uiOutput, the alert does show up, but independently of the option that is selected in Show alert?, as expected.

So the only conjecture I have so far is that bsAlert does not work within renderUI, but any insights would be appreciated!

ui.R

library(shiny)
library(shinyBS)

shinyUI(basicPage(
  radioButtons(inputId = "show_alert", "Show alert?",
               choices = c("Show alert" = TRUE,
                           "Do not show alert" = FALSE)),

  uiOutput("errorAlert")
))

server.R

library(shiny)
library(shinyBS)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  createAlert(session, inputId = "alert_anchor",
              title = "TITLE GOES HERE",
              message = "MESSAGE GOES HERE",
              type = "info",
              dismiss = TRUE,
              block = FALSE,
              append = TRUE
  )

  output$errorAlert <- renderUI({
    if (input$show_alert) {
      bsAlert(inputId = "alert_anchor")
    } else {
      return(NULL)
    }
  })

})

messages.subject: How to increase memory size for downloadHandler in Shiny?
messages.subject_clean: How to increase memory size for downloadHandler in Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
Hi All -

When running Shiny, I get the message that "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space" when the download function is called. It works when the data file is smaller; but all of the tables combined should be less than 5,000 rows and 15 columns for the instance I'm looking at. Can someone help me make my downloadHandler functional with this kind of file size? Thanks!
*# server.R*

library(XLConnect)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  ... (filtering operation on a data frame to create multiple sub tables)

  output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(

    filename = function() {paste(input$category,"_raw_token_data.xlsx")},

    content = function(file){
      fname <- paste(file,"xlsx",sep=".")
      wb <- loadWorkbook(fname, create = TRUE)
      createSheet(wb, name = "-terms")
      createSheet(wb, name = "+terms")
      createSheet(wb, name = "-tokens")
      createSheet(wb, name = "+tokens")
      createSheet(wb, name = "test_stats")
      writeWorksheet(wb, raw()$filter_neg, sheet = "-terms")
      writeWorksheet(wb, raw()$filter_kw, sheet = "+terms")
      writeWorksheet(wb, df()$neg_raw, sheet = "-tokens")
      writeWorksheet(wb, df()$rel_raw, sheet = "+tokens")
      writeWorksheet(wb, df()$test_raw, sheet = "test_stats")
      saveWorkbook(wb)
      file.rename(fname,file)
    }

  ) # closing for downloadHandler

}) # closing for shinyServer

Jonathan

In the code below the selection defaults to "a" and after viewing "a" or "b" then "c" will not show. shinyUI(fluidPage(

  selectInput("foo", label = h3("Select box"),

              selected = 1),

  hr(),
  fluidRow(column(12,
           dygraphOutput("plotdat")),
           dataTableOutput("tab"))

))

  dd <- reactive({

    #  Get data

                  "2" = cbind(ldeaths, fdeaths, mdeaths),
                  "3" = cbind(ldeaths, fdeaths, mdeaths))

        dySeries("fdeaths") %>%
        dyAxis("x", rangePad = 20) %>%
        dyAxis("y", valueRange = c(0, max(dd()))) %>%

messages.subject: Serial triggering of Plots in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Serial triggering of Plots in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Consider a complete app in Shiny. With multiple navbars, tabsets and plots.

What I need to build is a SEPARATE bottom info pane containing some information relevant to each of the rendered plots. This info depends on the actual data in the plotted chart.

So here is what I want to do Step1: user enters an input. Step2: Update the relevant plot Step3: compute relevant data needed for bottom pane and store in a global variable) Step4: once step3 IS COMPLETE, I want it to trigger an update of the bottom Pane

I tried to make the bottom pane AND the plot reactive to user input. BUT this may not guarantee that the plot rendering got a chance to update the data for info pane.

Any tips would be greatly appreciated.

thanks

Minimal EXAMPLE is here. NOTE - I know that I could make clusters a reactive "object". But the deal is that the myPlotInfo object is updated deep inside various functions. Hence it is not easily calculatable outside.

Server.R
source(util.R)
library(shiny)

myPlotInfo<-iris #setting inital value

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

 output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
 plotFunction(iris,input$xcol, input$ycol,input$clusters )
})

output$myTable<-renderDataTable({
  myPlotInfo
})

})

ui.R
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
 headerPanel('Iris k-means clustering'),
 sidebarPanel(
  selectInput('xcol', 'X Variable', names(iris)),
  selectInput('ycol', 'Y Variable', names(iris),
            selected=names(iris)[[2]]),
  numericInput('clusters', 'Cluster count', 3,
             min = 1, max = 9)
 ),
mainPanel(
 plotOutput('plot1'),
 dataTableOutput("myTable")
)

))

util.R
plotFunction<-function(dat,x,y,n){
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 0, 1))
selectedData<-dat[, c(x, y)]
clusters <- kmeans(selectedData,n)
myPlotInfo<<-clusters
plot(selectedData,
     col = clusters$cluster,
     pch = 20, cex = 3)
    points(clusters$centers, pch = 4, cex = 4, lwd = 4)
}

I have posted this at http://stackoverflow.com/questions/27919419/serial-triggering-of-plots-in-shiny also.

I am new to setting up the server side of things, so if my issue isn't clear, I am more than happy to provide more detail.

Thanks a lot for all your help.

You'd have to put options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE) at the top of your server.R or in a global.R file if you want it to work when deployed. But if you're expecting a lot of traffic for your app, I don't recommend it--the reactlog only grows in size, it never shrinks, and also adds runtime overhead to every reactive computation. Best to use it for testing then re-deploy with it disabled.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server not sourcing server.R until web page is accessed?
messages.body_plain:
An app that has 30-45 minute startup time is far outside the bounds of what we designed Shiny Server for. Have you considered doing the loading and preprocessing in a separate R process (managed by cron) outside of the Shiny app, and having it save its results in an .Rds file? Then the Shiny app can just refer to that .Rds file and load very quickly. This is a good general principle for Shiny: since doing computation in a Shiny app means a user is sitting there waiting, you want to preprocess/precompute/aggregate/summarize as much as you can offline.

You can even use reactiveFileReader so that even while the Shiny app is running, when the .Rds file is updated by the cron job, the data updates reactively--no need to restart the app.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server not sourcing server.R until web page is accessed?
messages.body_plain:
Being outside of the shinyServer(function) call but still in server.R means that it will be done once each time the Shiny app starts, which is different than when Shiny Server starts. The Shiny Server process is intended to be long-lived; it starts and stops Shiny apps (each of which runs in a different process, or even multiple processes in the case of Shiny Server Pro) as users come and go.

By default, Shiny Server is configured to assume that Shiny apps are relatively cheap to start and stop; it starts apps on demand and stops them just a few seconds after the last visitor to that app leaves.

messages.body_plain:
The usual way shiny displays the outcome is to insert it into a <pre> tag.
Now, the output I would like to display is sometimes longer (horizontally) than the width of the pre tag, so what I would like is to have a horizontal bar when this happens.

It probably isn't a shiny issue, but shiny uses <pre>... hence my question here.

By default (as far as I read), the <pre> tag uses word wrapping, which makes no sense with code and formatted text output.

Is there a way to enforce the <pre> tag *not* to do word wrapping?
Alternatively, can shiny use a different HTML tag to display the output?

Thanks,
Adrian

actionButton("clickBtn", "Click")

In the server.R file I have
library(shiny)
clickCounter <- 0
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$clickCount <- renderText({
    input$clickBtn
    clickCounter <- isolate(clickCounter + 1)
    clickCounter
    })

})

First of all, when the app loads the textOutput displays 1 and not 0. Secondly, nothing happens to the clickCounter when I click the button. I wanted to increase the number in textOutput("clickCount") by 1 every time the button is clicked.. is it possible or am I chasing windmills? :)

Thanks,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Counting button clicks
messages.subject_clean: Counting button clicks
messages.body_plain:
Hi Denis!

Not chasing windmills at all!  You just need to use the fact that the actionButton variable is already a counter that's initialized at zero.   The following should do what you want:

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(responsive = FALSE
    ,fluidRow(style = "padding-bottom: 20px;"
      ,column(width=6,
        textOutput("clickCount")
      )
      ,column(width=6,

        actionButton("clickBtn", "Click")

      )
    )
  )
  ,server = function(input, output, session) {
    output$clickCount <- renderText({
        input$clickBtn
    })
  }
  ,options = list(height = 500)
)

messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am working on a Shiny app to plot an interactive heatmap of some data, which requires ui.R and server.R to share data.  Basically, the idea is, the user selects mouse strains and brain regions that they want to plot by selecting the strains and regions of interest using two checkboxGroupInputs -- one for the strains, and one for the regions.  The user then clicks on a button to recalculate and replot the heatmap using the selected strains and regions.  I want to create a UI where the checkboxGroupInput options depend on the data loaded in server.R (in other words, I don't want to hard code the row names and column names because I want to eventually extend this to be a generic heatmap app).  Basically, one checkboxGroupInput would have row names and the other checkboxGroupInput would have column names of the main server.R data set.  Here's how I've been doing it:

# server.R

library(gplots)

#creates a dataset of effect sizes for each mouse strain * region and creates a data frame called mousedata
source('helpers.R')
source('loaddata.R')
mousedata = alleffects(datadefs)
mousedatamat = as.matrix(mousedata)

shinyServer(
  function(input, output) {

    #renderUI is used to produce a dynamic UI
    output$regions <- renderUI({
      checkboxGroupInput(inputId = 'regions',
                         label = h3('Brain Regions'),
                         choices = colnames(mousedata),
                         selected = colnames(mousedata))
    })
    output$strains <- renderUI({
      checkboxGroupInput(inputId = 'strains',
                         label = h3('Mouse Strains'),
                         choices = rownames(mousedata),
                         selected = rownames(mousedata))
    })

    output$heatmap = renderPlot({
      # Take a dependency on input$recalculate
      input$recalculate

      # Use isolate() to avoid dependency on input$strains and input$regions
      mousedatamat = as.matrix(mousedata[isolate(input$strains), isolate(input$regions)])
      nr = dim(mousedatamat)[1]
      nc = dim(mousedatamat)[2]

#       if (length(isolate(input$strains)) >= 2 & length(isolate(input$regions)) >= 2) {
        heatmap.2(mousedatamat, distfun=jdfs, col=bluered, margins=c(8,14), trace="none", cexRow = 0.2 + 2/log10(nr), cexCol = 0.2 + 2/log10(nc), density.info <http://density.info>="histogram", keysize=0.8, symkey=TRUE, symbreaks=TRUE)
#       }
    })
  }
)

# ui.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  fluidRow(column(12, plotOutput(outputId = 'heatmap', height = "650px"))),

  hr(),

  fluidRow(
    column(4, uiOutput('strains')),

    column(4, uiOutput('regions')),

    column(4, actionButton('recalculate', 'Recalculate'))
  )
))

When I run the app, the error I get is:
Error in heatmap.2(mousedatamat, distfun = jdfs, col = bluered, margins = c(8,  :
  `x' must have at least 2 rows and 2 columns

It's like my server.R file doesn't understand how to get the selected checkboxes from input$strains or input$regions.  Any help would be greatly appreciated!

P.S. Another thought I had was defining mousedata in global.R, but I was wondering whether global.R runs before server.R or how that would work.

Cheers

My code consists from:

ui.R
fileInput('portfolioFile', 'Choose portfolio file')

server.R
mainData <- reactive({

  if (is.null(input$portfolioFile)) return(NULL)

  read.csv((input$portfolioFile)$datapath, header=T, sep=";")
})

The problem here is, that fileInput does not update the input$portfolioFile value, even if the file was updated.
In order to reload the file, I need to choose a dummy file in fileInput dialog box first, and then click 'Choose portfolio file' again and point to my updated input file. Is there a better way to tell Shiny to reload an input?

You don't need to use actionButton, just make an HTML <a> tag right in your ui.R:

tags$a(class="btn btn-default", href="{url}", "{description}")

I wasn't sure from your question whether you wanted it in a new window, if so then also include target="_blank" as an argument.

messages.subject: Re: renderUI not working between server.R and ui.R
messages.subject_clean: renderUI not working between server.R and ui.R
messages.body_plain:
Easiest thing to do is move mousedata to global.R. The code in global.R is guaranteed to run before either ui.R or server.R, and any variables it declares are accessible from either file. So then you can get rid of both uiOutputs and there should never be invalid values for input$strains or input$regions.

It also looks to me like you don't need the top-level `mousedatamat = as.matrix(mousedata)`, as this value is never read but always created as a local variable within the renderPlot code.

Just out of intellectual curiousity--or if for some other reason mousedata couldn't be moved to global.R--I bet you could do something like this at the top of your renderPlot:

if (is.null(isolate(input$strains))) {
  input$strains # take a dependency on input$strains
  validate(FALSE) # abort rendering this time
}
if (is.null(isolate(input$regions))) {
  input$regions # take a dependency on input$regions
  validate(FALSE) # abort rendering this time
}

This will cause renderPlot to retry each time input$strains / input$regions changes, but only until they both have values.

> This seems like a simple problem and there should be a simple solution for it.  The crux is that my UI elements depend on data in server.R, but then server.R depends on the values of those UI elements.

messages.subject: Re: renderUI not working between server.R and ui.R
messages.subject_clean: renderUI not working between server.R and ui.R
messages.body_plain:
It's a subtle thing, but each time a renderXXX or reactive expression runs, it re-establishes its reactive dependencies from scratch. That is to say, at any given moment that output will rely on input$strain only if the *most recent invocation* of the output actually read input$strain (without isolate).

I found a solution by myself which may be useful for others. I decreased the size of the panel in which the table is visible bij imposing a smaller width of this panel. See the code below

library(shiny)
res <- data.frame(1,2,3)
runApp(list(
  ui = fluidPage(

    column(4,

    dataTableOutput("mytable"))

  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$mytable = renderDataTable(res, options =
                                       list(lengthchange = FALSE, searching = FALSE, info = FALSE, paging = FALSE,
                                            processing = FALSE, ordering = FALSE)
    )
  }
))

messages.subject_clean: To show labels on scatterplot with mouse click
messages.body_plain:
If you're trying to add interactivity to a plot created with base functions or ggplot2, yes, you have to do some fancy calculations and it's unlikely to be worth while.  You will find it easier if you swap to a different means of generating the graphic, using a package like {ggvis}, {googleVis} or {rcharts}.  If you're used to ggplot2 you'll find the transition to ggvis easiest.  googleVis is the most mature of the three but has some idiosyncratic data shape requirements and customisation/polishing often takes you straight into javascript; rcharts opens up a big world of options but doesn't have a consistent approach or enough documentation yet.  Whichever you choose you can still have Shiny deliver the fundamental interactivity, and the ggvis or whatever provides micro-interactivity (ie tooltips).  In fact ggvis works with Shiny in the background server-side even for tooltips but this doesn't seem to impact too much on performance.

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the concern , I have solved the problem.
I assign the checked rows of different tables to separate variable.
Because the original codes :

Shiny.onInputChange('rows1', $(this).add('tr td input:checkbox:checked').

send the checked rows of all interactive tables to the variable input$rows1

For example:
    addCheckboxButtons <- paste0('<input type="checkbox" name="check1" selected= "', mymtcars$id, '"  ', mymtcars$id, '" value= "', mymtcars$id, '">',"")
    Shiny.onInputChange('rows1', $(this).add('tr td input:checkbox[name=check1]:checked').

The same changes should be done for the second interactive tables.

Hope it is helpful to other people.

Jie

I recommend you use RStudio and put a browser() call at the beginning of that big renderDataTable() block. Then you can step through the execution one line at a time and hopefully see where you're going wrong.

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm working on a dynamic UI in a Shiny app I'm creating.  Basically, I'm trying to implement a "select/deselect all" checkboxInput, which dynamically selects/deselects another checkboxGroupInput's selected values.  I got this to work pretty easily, by creating a renderUI component in server.R and a uiOutput component in ui.R.  The problem now is that I don't know how to access the selection from uiOutput, which I need for rendering a plot in server.R.  Here's the code (omitting irrelevant lines of code):

ui.R

fluidRow(
  column(12, checkboxInput(inputId = 'selectAllStrains', label = 'Select/Deselect all strains', value = TRUE)),
)

fluidRow(
  column(12, uiOutput('selectStrains'))
)

server.R

output$selectStrains = renderUI({
      if (input$selectAllStrains == TRUE) {
        checkboxGroupInput(inputId = 'strains',
                           label = h3('Mouse Strains'),
                           choices = rownames(mousedata),
                           selected = rownames(mousedata))
      } else {
        checkboxGroupInput(inputId = 'strains',
                           label = h3('Mouse Strains'),
                           choices = rownames(mousedata),
                           vector(mode="character", length=0))
      }
    })

Here's the server.R component that requires the data from the uiOutput in ui.R.

output$heatmap = renderPlot({
      # Take a dependency on input$recalculate
      input$recalculate

      # Use isolate() to avoid dependency on input$strains and input$regions
      mousedatamat = as.matrix(mousedata[isolate(input$selectStrains), isolate(input$regions)])
      nr = dim(mousedatamat)[1]
      nc = dim(mousedatamat)[2]

      heatmap.2(mousedatamat, distfun=jdfs, col=bluered, margins=c(8,14), trace="none", cexRow = 0.2 + 2/log10(nr), cexCol = 0.2 + 2/log10(nc), density.info="histogram", keysize=0.8, symkey=TRUE, symbreaks=TRUE)

    })

Note here that input$recalculate is just an action button, input$regions is basically the same as strains, but not dynamic, and mousedatamat is just some data that is loaded in global.R.  I've tried accessing input$selectStrains and input$strains, and neither one works for me.  Specifically, I'm getting the error:

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7298
Error in heatmap.2(mousedatamat, distfun = jdfs, col = bluered, margins = c(8,  :
  `x' must have at least 2 rows and 2 columns

Thanks for the help!

messages.body_plain:
Initially I had posted question because I didn't see any solutions online after about a 30 minute Google search.  Just to let everyone know -- I resolved the issue.  What I did, was I added some error checking before the heatmap.2 call, like so:

server.R

if (min(dim(mousedatamat)) != 0) {

heatmap.2(mousedatamat, distfun=jdfs, col=bluered, margins=c(8,14), trace="none", cexRow = 0.2 + 2/log10(nr), cexCol = 0.2 + 2/log10(nc), density.info="histogram", keysize=0.8, symkey=TRUE, symbreaks=TRUE)

}

I should also note that when you generate a dynamic UI component in server.R and display it in ui.R with a uiOutput call, to refer to its values in server.R you need to use the inputId of the dynamic UI component you specified in server.R, NOT the outputId in uiOutput.  So in fact my initial post was incorrect because it really should have been isolate(input$strains), not isolate(input$selectStrains).

Cheers

messages.subject: Re: Shiny app trying to access SQLite db fails
messages.subject_clean: Shiny app trying to access SQLite db fails
messages.body_plain:
I found my mistake. Shiny apps on your local machine is not case sensitive but the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> web server is. The case of one the letters in my database file name was different in my code. This resulted in the app not looking through the database and thus giving "no such table" error.

>

> #OPEN LIBRARIES

> library("RSQLite")	#SQLITE LIBRARY
> library("DBI")
>
> #SET CONNECTION TO EXISTING SQLITE DATABASE
> sqlite <- dbDriver("SQLite")	#LOAD DRIVER
> candb <- dbConnect(sqlite, dbname= "WaterQuality_STEP_V8.sqlite")	#LOAD DB

> #IMPORT ALL DISTINCT CONSTITUENT NAMES FROM DATABASE

>

messages.body_plain:
Beginner here which would be very grateful for any assistance with the following.

I'm hoping to create a simple data app which allows me to:
input 3 values (numerically between 1-11)
output a time series graph.

If this is not possible, would direction in creating a logit function be plausible?

I know 3 values is scant, but I can add on as demanded.

Here is what I have

ui.R
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(   headerPanel("Time Series"),   sidebarPanel(
textInput(inputId="text1", label = "Input Text1"),
textInput(inputId="text2", label = "Input Text2"),
textInput(inputId="text2", label = "Input Text2"),
numericInput('Data', 'Time series',
             min = 0, max = 11)   ),   mainPanel(
plotOutput('plot1')   ) ))

server.R
    require(graphics)
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  # Combine the selected variables into a new data frame
  selectedData <-         reactive({   ts <- reactive({
    ts(selectedData(), input$ts)   })
    output$plot1 <- renderText({as.numeric(input$text1), as.numeric(input$text2, as.numeric(input$text3})
      par(mar = c(6.1, 4.1, 0, 1))
      plot(selectedData(),
           col = ts()$ts,
           pch = 20, cex = 3))   })    })

messages.subject: Updating a Data Frame with User-input Values for use in Predict()
messages.subject_clean: Updating a Data Frame with User-input Values for use in Predict()
messages.body_plain:
I have a web app that takes a stored randomForest() model and updates it with user-input values.

It should then run `predict()` with the updated dataframe and model object.

I'm able to display the updated dataframe in my UI with no problem, which I've been doing as a troubleshooting step. However, whenever I try to use the dataframe with `predict()` it leads to an error. The current and longest-running error that I've been getting is

Error: variables in the training data missing in newdata
However, I'm pretty sure that the problem is not simply a difference in the column names, because:
I can see that they are the same
I can run setdiff() and confirm that they match
The column names and dataframe in general is just a direct (updated) subset of the training dataframe
When trying various changes to the code I get different errors or, in some cases, the results simply do no appear

You can see what I've been trying at this Stackoverflow post. There's also a link to both a minimal reproducible version of the problem and of the entire working version of my project.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/27909898/errors-in-using-predict-with-randomforest-in-shiny

Minimal, reproducible example: https://github.com/hack-r/troubleshooting_predictor_minimal

Here's the full reproducible code and data: https://github.com/hack-r/coursera_shiny

messages.subject: Temporary error messages during the computing process
messages.subject_clean: Temporary error messages during the computing process
messages.body_plain:
My shiny application has 2 main tabs and there are several sub tabs within each main tab.
The first main tab is mainly about importing data, processing data and then pass the updated data to the second main tab.
The second main tab will exploring the data on the new updated one.

It works without problems, except one small annoying thing.
There is a temporary messages appears on  second tabs, "Error: argument is of length zero".
This error is not a real error, because it appear only for a few seconds, then it disappears and the expected results come out.
I guess it's probably because it takes time to process the data in the first tab, before the first tab passes the updated data to the second one,  there is no input in the second tab, that's probably the reason of the error message?
After a few seconds and the second tab receives the updated data, the error message disappears.

Does anyone know how to hide this message and print the message something like "The data processing may take a few moments..."

I tried to use the function of withProgress, but it doesn't help, the error messages still appear, the waiting messages defined in withProgress function only shows after the error message disappears and starting to explore the updated data.

I don't know if my question is understandable, please feel free to let me know you doubts, I will try to explain.

Thanks in advance.

Jie

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the comment Joe. My reply is give below. In an attempt to avoid a complete thread-jacking, could you suggest a way to get the ip address from inside a shiny app? None of the things Lichang or I have tried have been successful so far. Is the process used to put the ip address into the access_log not accessible inside Shiny/R?

I agree with you about the limitations of an ip address as an identifier. Students, at least when they are campus, will have a unique ip. Still not ideal, I agree. It would be great if there was information in the session object that could identify a browser session and that would survive a browser refresh. This is important for me because a student might spend a lot of time running analyses in the app and would be very unhappy to lose it all due to an accidental tab close or refresh.

The way this works in my app now is that the user can load and save the state and won't lose state on browser refresh. To load and activate a previous state I use a browser refresh (I have a LOT of inputs so using something like updateXXX for all of them might be a hassle). Basically the state is dumped into the global environment and then pulled in when the browser is refreshed. Once that is done the global variables (data and inputs) are deleted. Perhaps cookies could work if they provide a reference label that could be used as input to something like get() in R.

It would be great if there was something in session$request that you could use to assign a user id. Sort of like http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/chat-room.html but then with (some) memory for the user, i.e., you keep the id after browser refresh.

Creating a login might be an option. Question: How would you access the user id? Would it be through session$request? If so, why would that work when other attempts have not? I looked at the documentation but there is not much mentioned about this as far as I can tell.

Thanks Joe

messages.subject_clean: Using FA icons in DataTables, without risking html injection attacks
messages.body_plain:
If html injection is a concern (and escape=F was dangerous), is there a recommended approach to show FA icons?  Is reducing the number of columns showing HTML (by passing their names or index position) the only mitigation?

Background: My Shiny report has Font Awesome <http://fortawesome.github.io/Font-Awesome/> icons included in the DataTable (see the attached image).  After upgrading Shiny from 0.10.2 to 0.11.0, the HTML in the cells is rendered only when escape=FALSE (as documented in the NEWS <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shiny/NEWS>, and Issue #627 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/627>).  The table doesn't reflect any user input, so I don't think there's a security concern for the current report.  But I'd like to know in general.

If it helps, the report is here http://shiny.ouhsc.edu/TfcbtPublic/Shiny/TherapistProgress/ (select a therapist tag, such as '27vk'), and the source code is here: https://github.com/OuhscBbmc/TfcbtPublic/tree/master/Shiny/TherapistProgress.

Also, should the new escape parameter be mentioned in the Shiny 0.11 migration notes <https://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/47880_ea85145527b84be7aabb86695f6d0230.html>?

messages.subject: New shiny app for business intelligence
messages.subject_clean: New shiny app for business intelligence
messages.body_plain: Shiny is a fantastic framework for building interactive and powerful applications. For the past few months I've been working on an app called shinyData to make it easy to perform common data analysis tasks (usually referred to as business intelligence). It's available on GitHub <https://github.com/yindeng/shinyData>, and it's also hosted at ShinyApps.io <https://roose.shinyapps.io/shinyData/>. Part of shinyData is essentially a front end to ggplot2 (you can read more about this aspect at my blog post here <https://shinydata.wordpress.com/2015/01/08/front-end-for-ggplot2/>), but it's intended to be much more than that. In a nutshell, what I envision to achieve is to integrate the features already available in various r packages to create an end-to-end solution to users who may or may not know r. All feedback are welcome.

Tonio

messages.subject: Annimate Scatter Plot, in Time
messages.subject_clean: Annimate Scatter Plot, in Time
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am working with financial data in R and wanted to animate the progression of a scatter plot, in time, using Shiny (if possible). For example, lets say I have a time series of 10 variables. Thus, for each day in the time series, I would like to scatter plot 10 data points on the y-axis, with the x-axis simply being an index from 1 to 10.  In addition, I would like the y-axis scaling to be fixed in time, so that not only is the shape of the line reflected, but it will also illustrate any "rising" or "dropping" of the line's level.

The following is a simple example with a short time series of 3 variables.

Date, Var1, Var2, Var3
01/01, 4, 5, 6
01/02, 4, 4, 4
01/03, 3, 3, 3
01/04, 3, 2, 1

In the above simple example, I would expect there to be 4 separate "frames" in the animation, with the following progression:
Scatter plot #1. upward sloping line, with the first point starting at 4
Scatter plot #2. zero slope line, with all points at 4
Scatter plot #3. zero slope line, with all points at 3 (i.e. if the y-axis is fixed, the line should appear to "drop")
Scatter plot #4. downward sloping line, with the first point starting at 3

The goal is to illustrate the evolution of the shape of a line, in addition to it's associated level on the y-axis (i.e. in the example above, the line "drops" from Scatter plot #2 to Scatter plot #3).

Thank you!

Integrating InCHlib into my Shiny app (InCHlib: http://openscreen.cz/software/inchlib/home/)
Allowing a user to drag a rectangle over the cells that they want to plot?
Creating a separate navbar page where you can enter tags for the x variable values and y variable values and generate plots accordingly (this is my backup plan; it's not as fancy or user friendly, but it would still work)

Thanks!

Cool. You can also accumulate results over time using Hadley's shinySignals package <https://github.com/hadley/shinySignals>:

randomLetter <- reactive({
  invalidateLater(1000, session)
  sample(LETTERS, 1)
})

randomLetters <- shinySignals::reducePast(randomLetter, c, NULL)

This creates a randomLetters reactive whose return value is an ever-growing list of letters. I use this technique in the new "crandash" demo:

messages.subject: problem starting (restarting) shiny-server after update
messages.subject_clean: problem starting (restarting) shiny-server after update
messages.body_plain:
Dear crew,

First, I did do a search on this topic.  I found one possibly-related entry but it was a different OS and slightly different situation and the answer did not seem to resolve my situation.

Issue --

I recently upgraded from shiny-server v1.2.0 to v1.3.0.  I believe that I followed the instructions in the administrator's guide under migrating and updating.

My shiny-server is running on a corporate Linux server that uses Red Hat Enterprise release 6.5.

I updated using rpm and shiny-server-1.3.0.403-rh5-x86_64.rpm
Prior to this, I also reinstalled the latest version of R (3.1.2) and the shiny package (0.11).  The system worked after updating R and shiny.

Prior to the update of shiny-server things were running pretty well.  Love the package.  And for a couple of days after the update things also seemed to be working reasonably well.  I started to have an issue after a stop/start of the server (using sudo stop, sudo start, and also tried sudo restart).  When I try to restart the shiny-server, I get the message:

"start: Unknown job: shiny-server"

I checked for the shiny-server.conf file in the /etc/shiny-server/ directory and it is there.

Is the issue maybe related to the change in the default hosting directory?  Or something else?

Thank you in advance for any guidance.

Cliff

messages.body_plain:
Cliff,

If running on Red Hat Enterprise release 6.5 (as you are), there should be 2 config files, with same names:
/etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
/etc/init/shiny-server.conf

You have the first one, which is for configuring runtime of Shiny Server.
The second one (missing from your system) is an Upstart file, for controlling stop/start of Shiny Server as a service.
I just tried the same binary on Red Hat Enterprise release 6.5, and it works fine. May be something went wrong during your installation. Do you mind uninstalling Shiny Server, and installing again using the same rpm. See if you get any errors during installation.

And please check for /etc/init/shiny-server.conf file after install is completed.

Fereshteh

renderDataTable needs to be passed another argument `escape = c(-1)` which means that column 1 should *not* be HTML escaped (but the other columns should). This is a change we made for security reasons, otherwise it could be dangerous to render data tables using untrusted data.

I've modified the code according to your comment:

ui.R

library(shiny)
# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel("my dataset"),

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      radioButtons("kollektiv", label = h1("Valg"),

                   choices = list("HGG4" = "fa35up",
                                  "HGG3" = "fa35down",
                                  "HGG3.5" = "fa35asis",
                                  "HGGexcluded" = "fa35out",
                                  "LGGvs.HGG" = "fahighlow"))),
    mainPanel(
                textOutput("text"),
                plotOutput("bubble")

            )
          )

))

server.R:

library(shiny)

#gliom <- read.csv("data/gliom_0801_1346.csv")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  falist <- list("fa35up"=c("2","3","4","4"), "fa35down"=c("2", "3","3","4"), "fa35asis"=c("2","3","3.5","4"), "fa35out"=c("2", "3", NA, "4"), "fahighlow"= c("2", "4", "4", "4"))
  output$text <- renderText({input$kollektiv})
  output$bubble <- renderPlot({
    factory <- factor(gliom$Rdx.new)
    levels(factory) <- falist[[input$kollektiv]]
    y <- factory
    x <- factor(gliom$Grade)

    gliom.heat <- as.data.frame(table(x,y, useNA="no"))
    ggplot(gliom.heat, aes(x, y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill =Freq), colour="black") + scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high ="steelblue")

  })

})

This works. Thanks for your help.

levels(factory) <- falist[[input$kollektiv]]

when

input$kollektiv

represented a numeric value it didn't work. It seemed not to select the right list element.
as a character value/label it selected the right list element and everything worked fine.
What's the reason for this?

Thanks for your help.

I recently discovered shinydashboard http://rstudio.github.io/shinydashboard/index.html and I wanted to see if I could modify my current shiny app to use it.

However I'm not sure how to get the server side to work, for Shiny, the function shinyServer wraps the code defining the server in the file server.R, and
shinyUI wraps the code defining the UI in ui.R and runApp() in Rstudio works.

Inspecting several source codes of example shinydashboard apps here: https://github.com/jcheng5/crandash

They don't use shinyServer(), and have files like global.R and the server code in server.R is simply contained in

function(input, output, session){} - no shinyServer() use.

What is the right way to use shinydashboard in an already existing app? The website only shows you how to use it for a single file app:

# app.R ##
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(),
  dashboardSidebar(),
  dashboardBody()
)

server <- function(input, output) { }

shinyApp(ui, server)

but doesn’t tell me what I need to do if I have separate files ui.R and server.R and so on to get it to work with runApp().

messages.subject: Re: Using Shiny and Shinydashboard
messages.subject_clean: Using Shiny and Shinydashboard
messages.body_plain:
Sorry for not explaining this. These two server.R files are identical:

# server.R 1
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
   ...
})

# server.R 2
function(input, output, session) {
   ...
}

As long as the server function is the last expression in server.R, the shinyServer call is now optional. The same is true for shinyUI in ui.R; it's optional as long as the last expression is your UI.

I thought about this some more, I think the right answer is to use history.replaceState in the browser to "tag" the browser with a session ID. I'll see if I can come up with an example for you.

None of the things Lichang or I have tried have been successful so far. Is the process used to put the ip address into the access_log not accessible inside Shiny/R?

>
> I agree with you about the limitations of an ip address as an identifier. Students, at least when they are campus, will have a unique ip. Still not ideal, I agree. It would be great if there was information in the session object that could identify a browser session and that would survive a browser refresh. This is important for me because a student might spend a lot of time running analyses in the app and would be very unhappy to lose it all due to an accidental tab close or refresh.
>
> The way this works in my app now is that the user can load and save the state and won't lose state on browser refresh. To load and activate a previous state I use a browser refresh (I have a LOT of inputs so using something like updateXXX for all of them might be a hassle). Basically the state is dumped into the global environment and then pulled in when the browser is refreshed. Once that is done the global variables (data and inputs) are deleted. Perhaps cookies could work if they provide a reference label that could be used as input to something like get() in R.
>
> It would be great if there was something in session$request that you could use to assign a user id. Sort of like http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/chat-room.html but then with (some) memory for the user, i.e., you keep the id after browser refresh.

messages.subject: bug: width parameter in sliderInput does nothing (possibly others too)
messages.subject_clean: bug: width parameter in sliderInput does nothing (possibly others too)
messages.body_plain:
I tried to change the 'width' parameter of a sliderInput, only to find that it did nothing.
Investigating the code showed me why; width is never used!
Probably remove this parameter from the documentation.
I used this workaround

gsub('form-group shiny-input-container"',
          'form-group shiny-input-container" style="width: 100%;"',
           sliderInput("barNum",
           label="Number of Bins",
           min=8,max=60,value=35))

messages.body_plain:
When you say the limit on uploads is 30MB, are you referring to the limits for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>?

If you are working with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, you will want the file that you are loading to be in the same directory (or a sub-directory) of the application.  Absolute paths are a problem because when you transfer an application up to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, it will only know about the directory that the application is in, and the sub-directories so any files that are references relative to your machine are not going to be in the same location on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

messages.subject: Re: Variable number of plots - reactive
messages.subject_clean: Variable number of plots - reactive
messages.body_plain:
Yes, it's quite straightforward. I believe this should work:

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  output$plots <- renderUI({
    lapply(seq_len(input$plotCount), function(x) {
      output[[paste0("plot", x)]] <- renderPlot({
        ...
      })
      plotOutput(paste0("plot", x))
    })
  })
})

On Fri, Jan 30, 2015 at 10:31 AM, Ben Ward <axolotl...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I've recently seen this example of generating multiple plot outputs programmatically:
>
> Here is functional code to make a variable number of plots based on the number of columns.  I suggest using this as a starting point, and adding small amounts of code until you pinpoint what exactly is breaking it.
>
> server.r:
> max_plots <- 100
> library(shinyIncubator)
>
> shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>
> sampletable=reactive({
> if(input$go<1)
> return()
>
> x1=c(106:110, 21:25)
> x2=c(101:105, 201:205)
> x3=c(21:25, 31:35)
> x4=c(51:60)
> input$go
> x=isolate(rbind(x1,x2,x3,x4))
>
> x
> })
>   # Insert the right number of plot output objects into the web page
>   output$plots <- renderUI({
>     plot_output_list <- lapply(1:ncol(sampletable()), function(i) {
>
>       plotname <- paste("plot", i, sep="")
>       plotOutput(plotname, height = 280, width = 250)
>     })
>
>     # Convert the list to a tagList - this is necessary for the list of items
>     # to display properly.
>     do.call(tagList, plot_output_list)
>   })
>
>   # Call renderPlot for each one. Plots are only actually generated when they
>   # are visible on the web page.
>   for (i in 1:max_plots) {
>     # Need local so that each item gets its own number. Without it, the value
>     # of i in the renderPlot() will be the same across all instances, because
>     # of when the expression is evaluated.
>     local({
>       my_i <- i
>       plotname <- paste("plot", my_i, sep="")
>
>       output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot({
>         plot(sampletable()[,my_i], sampletable()[,my_i],
>              xlim = c(min(sampletable()[,my_i]), max(sampletable()[,my_i])),
>              ylim = c(min(sampletable()[,my_i]), max(sampletable()[,my_i])),
>              main = "look at all those things"        )
>       })
>     })
>   }
> })
>
> ui.r
>
> library(shinyIncubator)
> shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
>
>   headerPanel("Dynamic number of plots"),
>
>   sidebarPanel(
>     sliderInput("n", "this isn't used, I used the ncol function instead, but feel free to move the slider for fun.", value=1, min=1, max=5),
>   actionButton("go", "Update")
>   ),
>
>   mainPanel(
>     # This is the dynamic UI for the plots
>     uiOutput("plots")
>   )
> ))
>
> My question is, how easy is this to be made reactive? Say instead of max_plots, there is an input value that A). is evaluated to determine the number of plots, and prep the renderPlot elements, and then B). send them the appropriate plots generated? I wondered if this might be done with two reactive statements? One depends on the input variable and then makes the renderPlot elements for the UI, then the code to provide those with the plots is in a reactive element that depends on the previous?
>
> Thanks,
> Ben.
>

messages.subject: Re: Disableing MathJax Zoom in shiny app
messages.subject_clean: Disableing MathJax Zoom in shiny app
messages.body_plain:
Wanted to answer my own question for other people in the future.

the `renderPlot` function has a parameter for `width` and `height` that are set to 'auto' by default.

You can give it a value (in pixels) to have the plots not resize itself when the browser window is resized.
There is also a `res` (for resolution) that is set to 72 by default

A sample of using the `width` and `height` parameters:

    output$facet_plots <- renderPlot({
        plots_facet[1]
    }, width = 825, height = 600)

- Dan

>
> I've created a shiny app with ggplot.
> Is there a way to disable the mathjax zoom when the browser window is resized?
> The automatic resizing is making the application less responsive and slow.
>
>
>
> Thanks,
> Dan

messages.body_plain:
There must be a way to remove the FixedHeader of the oTable in a tab and then create a new one when user clicks on the other Tab.

On Tuesday, 16 December 2014 06:51:37 UTC-6, Jie Song wrote:
> Hi Yihui
> I tried the example you gave in my own application.
> Since I have several main and sub tabs, I found that the head of the table appears on all the tabs, which is quite annoying.

>
> Thanks very much.
> Jie
>
> 在 2014年2月25日星期二UTC+1下午10时49分22秒，Yihui Xie写道：
> > Hi,
> >
> > I just added experimental support for this in the development version:
> > https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/
> >
> > You need to download the FixedHeader plugin from
> > http://datatables.net/extras/ and put dataTables.fixedHeader.js under
> > www/ (if you put it in other directories, you need to adjust the path
> > in tags$script() below accordingly). Then this should work:
> >
> > # ui.R
> > shinyUI(fluidPage(
> >     dataTableOutput('tab1'),
> >     tags$head(
> >       tags$style(type='text/css', '.fixedHeader table.table thead
> > .sorting { background-color: #eee; }'),
> >       tags$script(src='dataTables.fixedHeader.js')
> >     )
> > ))
> >
> > # server.R
> > shinyServer(function(input, output) {
> >     output$tab1 = renderDataTable(iris, callback='function(oTable) {
> > new FixedHeader(oTable); }')
> > })
> >
> > Please test it if you can. Thanks!
> >
> > Regards,
> > Yihui
> >
> >
> > On Fri, Feb 21, 2014 at 12:13 AM, Aaron Ouyang
> > <aaron....@glamour-sales.com.cn> wrote:

> > > datatables site as below and make it work on the table output?
> > >
> > > /*
> > >  * Example initialisation
> > >  */
> > > $(document).ready( function () {
> > >     var table = $('#example').dataTable();
> > >     new $.fn.dataTable.FixedHeader( table );
> > > } );
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > Does RStudio consider include the "Fixed Header" as an option for
> > > rednerDataTable()? This will help many people.
> > >
> > > Thanks.
